To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HIV is not completely suppressed in semen of HIV-infected MSM despite HAART, and that STI and genital inflammation are associated with increased risk of HIV shedding in semen.
STI/urethral inflammation and unprotected anal intercourse with an HIV-infector partner were independent predictors of HIV shedding in semen.
1) HAART does not completely suppress genital shedding and transmission of HIV in MSM, and 2) STIs and genital inflammation may promote HIV transmission in MSM, even when they are using HAART.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of inflammation in the genital tract in the context of HAART.
the effects of HIV and its associated infections on the male reproductive system and semen quality.
the development of a new generation of highly active antiretrovirals (HARV) that can be used in combination with HAART to prevent HIV transmission.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HAART does not completely suppress the shedding of HIV into semen of HIV-infected MSM.
the use of HAART does not completely suppress the presence of HIV in semen, even in men who have undetectable HIV RNA levels in blood plasma.
the use of HAART does reduce HIV transmission, but not completely, in HIV-infected men having sex with men.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIV-infected MSM who are on HAART and are sexually active are still at risk for transmission of HIV to their partners.
HAART is not a complete cure.

The main takeaway from our work is that
HIV-infected men on HAART who are sexually active should be counseled that they may still be at risk for transmitting the virus through unprotected anal sex.
HIV can persist in the male genital tract despite HAART, and that STIs and genital inflammation are associated with increased seminal HIV shedding.
HIV-infected men on stable HAART can still have detectable HIV in semen, and that this is associated with genital inflammation, STIs, and unprotected sex.
